quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When starting your motorcycle, the engine should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral.
questions.explanation: Always start your motorcycle with the transmission in neutral. Most motorcycles have a neutral light on the dashboard that turns on when the engine is ready to start and the bike is in neutral.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull to the side of the road until the rain stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it rains, the center of the lane becomes slippery with oil. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the safest choice.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride at speeds faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead on the road while riding. This helps you spot dangers early so you can react before you reach them.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
Should not be a concern, since the motorcycle has two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a significant contributing factor to many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Learning proper braking technique is essential for safe riding.

questions.question: In the center of a traffic lane, there is usually an oily strip. Motorcyclists should:

options.text: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
Not worry about the oil and grease buildup.
Search for the lane with the smallest amount of oil and grease buildup.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid riding on the oil and grease buildup.
questions.explanation: Stay away from the oily strip in the center of the lane. This strip is usually only about two feet wide, so you can ride on either side of it and still be in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If using saddlebags to carry a load, you should:

options.text: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
Unevenly distribute weight into the saddlebags.
Place as much weight as possible into one saddlebag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load the bags as evenly as possible.
questions.explanation: Put equal weight in each saddlebag. If one bag is heavier than the other, the motorcycle may drift to one side.

questions.question: A solid white line on the side of the road indicates:

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to be out of the way of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake is ineffective on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid making sudden moves, as doing so could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden changes in speed or direction cause skids. Make smooth, gradual movements when speeding up, shifting gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.correctAnswerText: The middle portion
questions.explanation: Oil and debris from cars and trucks collect in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting while turning can cause sudden power changes that make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to prevent skidding.

questions.question: When should you inspect your motorcycle for safety?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Always inspect your motorcycle before riding. Small problems on a motorcycle are more dangerous than small problems on a car.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when towing a trailer. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, where is the best place to ride?

options.text: On the right side of the lane.
On the edge of the road.
In the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Roads are slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil left by cars. Ride in the tire tracks of cars ahead of you for better grip.

questions.question: Where is the biggest danger of conflict with other vehicles?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: The biggest danger is at intersections. Oncoming cars turning left in front of motorcycles cause the most conflicts.

questions.question: What can cause motorcycle collisions?

options.text: Sounding the horn at the wrong time

questions.correctAnswerText: Tailgating
questions.explanation: Following too closely behind another vehicle can cause motorcycle collisions. Always keep a safe distance when riding behind others.

questions.question: What should you do when changing lanes?

options.text: Your mirrors show you everything you need to see.
Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
Signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot in addition to using mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, even after checking your mirrors.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle, what should you do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes helps you stop quickly and safely.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during braking, release the front brake right away, then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Skip the stop line and move forward to get a better view.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: Stop where the stop line indicates. Then edge forward and stop again just before the cross traffic lane. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to see if traffic is coming. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: The body removes alcohol at what rate?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. This rate varies by person. Do not ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Why is stopping in a turn difficult?

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
The rider is focused on the turn, not on braking.
The brakes do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be careful. When the motorcycle leans, some traction is used for the turn. This leaves less traction for stopping.

questions.question: As you drink more alcohol, your ability to safely ride:
questions.correctAnswerText: Decreases.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills get worse as you drink more alcohol. Do not ride if you have consumed any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When riding at night, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.
